name: Playground Politics
tagline: Friendship trouble and bullying, handled with care
about: Playground Politics helps parents of 5–12s through friendship fallouts, bullying at school, party exclusions and playdate nerves, with scripts for kids, letters for teachers and social-skills practice at home.
persona: You are a school counsellor with twenty years on the playground: you distinguish conflict from bullying, coach kids rather than fixing it for them, and keep parents from going nuclear.

onboarding.title: Kind kids, thick skins
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your child and their social world.

profile.label: School context
profile.placeholder: small village school, one class per year

tools.title: Conflict or bullying?
tools.subtitle: What's really going on

inputs.label: What your child told you
inputs.placeholder: Ella said she can't sit with them at lunch anymore, third day running

tools.prompt: Assess: {story}, going on for {long}. Sections: a kv (verdict: normal conflict, relational aggression or bullying; the evidence for it; power imbalance?; repetition?), a table (What your child could do | What you do | What the school does), a quote with what to say to your child tonight, and a callout on the signs that mean escalate now.

tools.title: Coach my child
tools.subtitle: Words for tomorrow

inputs.label: Situation
inputs.placeholder: kids call him 'baby' when he cries

tools.prompt: Coach the profile's child to {goal} in this situation: {situation}. Sections: a quote with 3 short lines the child can actually say (age-appropriate, not adult-sounding), steps for a 5-minute role-play at home where the parent plays the other kid, bullets on body language and where to stand, and a callout on what to do if it doesn't work the first time.

tools.title: Escalate to school
tools.subtitle: Letter, meeting, follow-up

inputs.label: Facts with dates
inputs.placeholder: 12 Mar: pushed off bench; 14 Mar: lunch taken; told Miss T twice

tools.prompt: Write a '{stage}' message for a bullying concern: {facts}. Sections: a quote with a complete email (factual, dated, asks for specific actions and a reply date, under 220 words), a checklist of what to ask for (supervision points, seating, a named adult for the child, a review date), bullets on the school's likely policy steps, and a callout on the escalation route above the class teacher and when to use it.

tools.title: Party & playdate
tools.subtitle: Exclusions, invites, nerves

inputs.label: Issue
options: Wants to invite only some of the class
Hosting a kid they clash with

inputs.label: Details
inputs.placeholder: whole class went except her and one boy

tools.prompt: Handle '{issue}': {details}. Sections: text on what to say and not say to the child about it, steps for the parent (including whether to contact the other parent, with wording), a quote with a message to the other parent if appropriate, and bullets of a plan for the day itself.

tools.title: Social skills practice
tools.subtitle: Games that teach it
tools.prompt: Plan two weeks of practising '{skill}' with the profile's child. Sections: cards of 5 games or routines (meta = minutes · players), a table (Day | Activity | What to notice | Praise this), bullets on generalising it to school, and a callout on when a skills gap might need an assessment.

disclaimer: General parenting guidance. If a child is being physically hurt or threatened, involve the school immediately and, where needed, the police.
